<WORKER-BRIEF>

**Task: audit finding 2A on flutter/flutter#196561 (your branch `vcfix-manifest-fallback`, current head `7233196849d`)**

An audit agent built a playground app against this PR in 28 configurations. reidbaker asked that you act on its findings. Other findings will come to you in separate briefs. This brief covers only finding 2A. Here is the finding exactly as the audit wrote it, followed by the audit's method note:

> **Verification**: Every output APK in `build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/` and `build/app/outputs/apk/` was inspected with `aapt2 dump badging`.

> ### 2A. Following the error message's `-P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true` suggestion when no `versionCode` exists builds **un-installable APKs (`versionCode=''`)**
>
> When neither `android {}` nor `src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` sets a `versionCode`:
> - **Flutter 3.47**: Used `-1` (`variant.mergedFlavor.versionCode`) and silently built APKs with `versionCode='999'`, `'1999'`, `'3999'` (`1000 * abi + (-1)`).
> - **PR #196561**: Fails cleanly (big improvement!), and prints:
>   > `Set versionCode = flutter.versionCode in defaultConfig (or on each product flavor), or pass -P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true to keep one versionCode.`
>
> **Escape-Hatch Trap**
> If the developer follows the second suggestion on that exact project:
> ```bash
> flutter build apk --debug --split-per-abi -P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true
> ```
> the build **exits `0`** and writes `app-armeabi-v7a-debug.apk`, `app-arm64-v8a-debug.apk`, and `app-x86_64-debug.apk` with **`versionCode=''` (empty / missing in the compiled binary `AndroidManifest.xml`)**. `adb install` rejects those APKs on Android devices. Saying *"to keep one versionCode"* when no `versionCode` exists anywhere misleads the user into producing broken APKs.

**Treat this as input, not proof.** The method note says the APKs were only checked with `aapt2 dump badging`. Nothing says `adb install` was ever run. That makes the claim "`adb install` rejects those APKs" unverified. Make up your own mind on each point:

1. **Reproduce it.** Build a project where neither `android {}` nor `src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` sets `versionCode`. Run the exact command above against your branch. Record the exit code and the `aapt2 dump badging` output for each APK.
2. **Test the install claim yourself.** Run `adb install` on at least one of those APKs on an emulator or device. Record the exact output. A manifest with no `android:versionCode` may just default to 0 and install fine. If so, the "un-installable" part of the finding is wrong, and your report must say that.
3. **Compare against baselines** on the same project:
   - a plain `flutter build apk --debug` (no split). Does it also produce `versionCode=''`?
   - the same `--split-per-abi -P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true` command on Flutter 3.47, if you can run it.

   Suppose the flag only produces what a non-split build already produces. Then the PR does not introduce a broken-APK path, and what's left is the wording.
4. **Decide the fix on its merits.** Whatever the install result, the clause "to keep one versionCode" is misleading when no versionCode exists. Options:
   - (a) When no versionCode is found anywhere, keep the "set `versionCode = flutter.versionCode`" advice and leave out the force-flag suggestion. Offer that suggestion only when a versionCode exists that can be kept.
   - (b) Keep both suggestions, but reword the second so it states what really happens (no ABI offset is applied, and the APKs use whatever versionCode the manifest has).
   - (c) Also fail the build when the force flag is set and no versionCode exists. **Don't do (c) without asking me first.** It changes how an explicit opt-out flag behaves, which goes beyond this PR.

   My leaning is (a), unless step 2 or 3 shows a reason against it. If you pick something else, explain why.
5. **Test it.** Add or update a unit test that asserts the exact error text for the "no versionCode anywhere" case, and for the case where a versionCode exists, if your fix splits them. Run the Gradle plugin tests that cover this path, plus the relevant `flutter_tools` tests. Then re-run the step 1 command and confirm the new message is printed.
6. **Push to the `reidbaker-agent` fork** on `vcfix-manifest-fallback`. Merge, don't rebase. Don't push to `flutter/flutter`. If the PR description quotes the error message or describes the escape hatch, update it so it matches the new behavior.
7. **Don't post anything on GitHub about this finding.** It came from an internal audit, not a PR comment.

**Report back to me with:**
- Your verdict on 2A: changed, modified, or declined, with reasons. Give a separate verdict on the "un-installable" claim, backed by your `adb install` output.
- The commands you ran and the key output: exit codes, `aapt2` lines, `adb install` result, and the baseline comparisons.
- The old and new error message text, exactly.
- The new head SHA and the names of the tests you added or changed.

Don't call the PR ready. I'll review the fix diff and run the review passes before anything goes to reidbaker.
